newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's 1997 draft budget seen approved Sept 27.
newsitem.headline: Spain's 1997 draft budget seen approved Sept 27.

text.p: Spain's new conservative government is likely to approve its first budget by September 27, three days before it is legally required to present it to parliament, Economy Ministry sources told Reuters on Friday.

A draft of the 1997 budget, aimed at getting Spain into the first round of European economic and monetary union, is still under discussion. Adjustments to the measures are likely to fill the next three weeks, the sources said.
"There are still matters to be settled and conversations to take place," said an Economy Ministry source. "The numbers are as yet unknown."

The government is aiming for 2.3 percent growth of public spending in nominal terms, or a cut of three-tenths of a percentage point in real terms, Deputy Prime Minister Francisco Alvarez Cascos told a press conference last week.
"The basic aim...is that spending in government departments does not grow by more than 2.3 percent," he said.
The government needs to trim the public sector deficit by around one trillion pesetas to meet next year's three percent of gross domestic product target for Europe's monetary union.
